newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN KAMAZ TRUCKMAKER REVIEWING KKR AGREEMENT.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN KAMAZ TRUCKMAKER REVIEWING KKR AGREEMENT.

text.p: Russian heavy truck and vehicle maker KamAZ KMAZ.RTS said on Thursday its board of directors would take a decision on future cooperation with U.S. investment company Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co (KKR) in September.

KamAZ's head of public relations Nail Galiullin said the board had decided to review agreements signed with KKR which would give the financing company options on shares in return for attracting investment.
Galiullin did not say what moves KamAZ could make.
KKR was not available for comment.
The mid-1990s agreements were designed to attract investment to KamAZ from KKR and other Western investors.
A CentreInvest Securities report said that originally KKR-KamAZ deals had given KKR the possibility of acquiring a controlling stake in KamAZ.

But KKR appeared not to have attracted investment to meet agreement targets and a recent decision by KamAZ to transfer shares to the regional Tatarstan government put KKR's potential stake in question, it said.

KamAZ, located in the autonomous Tatarstan Republic in central European Russia, posted a pre-tax loss, calculated to Russian standards on an accruals basis, of 1.16 trillion roubles for 1996, after a loss of 520 billion roubles in 1995.
